request_context: A request to review a code change for security, data-safety and input-validation problems before it is approved or submitted, especially when it touches authentication, database mutations or calls across public API surfaces.

rules.source_quote: Information disclosure: stack trace, internal ID, or raw exception surfaced to caller
rules.outcome: Flags error responses that return stack traces, internal identifiers or raw exception text to callers as a serious problem that should block approval, and proposes returning a generic mapped error while logging details server-side.
rules.why: Leaked internals help attackers map the system and expose sensitive data.
rules.scenario_hint: Diff where an API handler catches an exception and returns its message or stack trace in the response body.

rules.source_quote: Non-atomic multi-item write without transaction (data corruption risk)
rules.outcome: Flags changes that write several related records in separate calls without making them all-or-nothing as a blocking problem, and suggests a transaction or equivalent atomic operation.
rules.why: A failure midway leaves partially written, inconsistent data.
rules.scenario_hint: Diff that updates two related database items in separate sequential calls.

rules.source_quote: Unconditional overwrite on a resource subject to concurrent writes
rules.outcome: Flags unconditional overwrites of records that concurrent requests may modify as a blocking problem, and proposes a conditional write or version check so a stale write is rejected.
rules.why: Concurrent writers silently clobber each other and corrupt state.
rules.scenario_hint: Diff that replaces a shared record with a plain put without any condition or version check.

rules.source_quote: Input used in a query before validation (injection or logic bypass risk)
rules.outcome: Flags user-supplied values, including decoded pagination cursors or opaque tokens, that reach a query without being validated first as a blocking problem, and proposes validating them before use.
rules.why: Unvalidated tokens allow injection or access to data the caller should not see.
rules.scenario_hint: Diff that base64-decodes a page token from the request and passes it directly into a database query.

rules.source_quote: Request payload logged at info/debug level
rules.outcome: Flags logging of full request or response payloads at routine log levels as a should-fix problem because they may contain sensitive data, and suggests logging only safe fields.
rules.why: Logs spread sensitive user data to systems with weaker access control.
rules.scenario_hint: Diff adding a log statement that dumps the whole incoming request body.

rules.source_quote: Write path with no test coverage
rules.outcome: Points out new or changed code that modifies stored data when no test exercises that write, and asks for a specific test.
rules.why: Untested writes let data-corrupting regressions ship unnoticed.
rules.scenario_hint: Diff adding a new write operation where the included tests only cover reads.

rules.source_quote: Map key accessed without existence guard
rules.outcome: Flags access to nested object or map keys without first checking that the parent exists, and proposes a guard or safe default.
rules.why: Missing parents cause runtime crashes on legitimate inputs.
rules.scenario_hint: Diff reading item['details']['owner'] where details may be absent.

rules.source_quote: Validate-then-act ordering violated (validation present but runs after side effect)
rules.outcome: Flags code where validation happens after a write, call or other side effect has already occurred, and proposes moving validation ahead of any business logic.
rules.why: Invalid input still causes side effects that cannot be undone.
rules.scenario_hint: Diff where a handler saves a record and then checks the request fields.

rules.source_quote: Integration wiring gap (handler registered but not connected to auth/middleware)
rules.outcome: Flags a newly added handler or route that is not connected to the router, authorization or middleware chain, noting that it may be unprotected or unreachable.
rules.why: An unwired endpoint can bypass authentication or silently never work.
rules.scenario_hint: Diff adding a new endpoint handler but no matching authorizer or route configuration.

rules.source_quote: Existing transaction helpers or batch-write utilities — flag reimplementation as a violation
rules.outcome: Notes when the change reimplements logic such as transactions, validation, error mapping or token handling that the codebase already provides in shared utilities, and recommends using the existing one.
rules.why: Bypassing shared utilities loses their safeguards and fragments behavior.
rules.scenario_hint: Diff hand-rolling cursor decoding although a shared encode/decode helper exists in the repository.

rules.source_quote: Every finding must make a case for blocking or conditioning approval.
rules.outcome: Each finding names the specific location, explains the defect and the risk it creates, and gives a concrete fix rather than vague advice.
rules.why: Vague findings waste the author's time and cannot be acted on.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to review a code change before approval.

rules.source_quote: Present findings as: CRITICAL → IMPORTANT → SUGGESTION.
rules.outcome: Findings are ordered from must-block issues to should-fix to optional improvements, with the groups clearly separated.
rules.scenario_hint: Any request to review a code change before approval.
